Khmelnytskyy New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Khmelnytska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. This cemetery emerged at the end of the 19th century, first appearing on a Russian map from the 1890s; its oldest preserved gravestone fragment is from the early 19th century, though this may have been relocated from an earlier, now-demolished Khmelnytskyi cemetery rather than reflecting this site's own founding date. Jews were present here from 1629 and suffered during the Khmelnytsky massacres of 1648–49; the community grew to 11,411 by 1897, supporting a hospital and nine synagogues, before a pogrom by Symon Petliura's forces killed 1,600 people in February 1919. The Jewish population peaked at 14,518 (38.7 percent of the town) in 1939. Winter 1941 brought two ghettos holding over 10,000 prisoners combined; the Jewish ghetto's liquidation in October 1942 killed 5,300 people, and the separate labor camp's roughly 9,000 prisoners were shot in two further actions that November and after.
